original_card.question: What explicit uniform stock envelope does the actual selected stopped producer supply at one bootstrap stage?
methods: Derive a source-bound reserve recurrence at the actual selected atom widths, separating parent stock from completed inner borrowing.
Find an exact missing implication or counterexample to a proposed selected-stage stock envelope.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Bind every coefficient and depth factor to the selected producer and state the width domain. Compare a proved envelope with the sufficient cutoff guard; a large numerical headroom or a historical m=120 coefficient is not a selected m=73 proof.

first_step.inspect: Read #1956/#1965/#1990 in the batch review and the stock-audit source boundary. Its actual selected coefficient remains uncomputed.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one of the fourteen recorded stages, pin its producer, and derive the parent reserve and depth coefficient. Stop with a precise source-level missing lemma if that coefficient cannot yet be bounded; do not rerun the already checked headroom arithmetic as a new result.
original_card.bottleneck_link: This reduces a concrete inherited implementation obligation without confusing unchanged kappa arithmetic with a completed theorem.
allowed_variations: One stage or one explicit reserve/depth implication.
An independently checked same-domain proof repair, retaining all remaining assumptions.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the historical 57604 or 252 allowance without a selected-producer binding.
Calling a conditional fit lemma a full outer-proof adoption.

actual_scope: For the frozen selected bootstrap receipt, do the remaining cutoff pairs s*L_j - L_{j-1} (native stages 4-7 and conservative stages 2-7) put every width-w call inside the previous stopped range, and does that choose the stock coefficient?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one stage. Native stage 2 has a conditional handoff (discussion comment 18949652) and native stage 3 has an audit (PR #2931); this note covers the ten remaining cutoff pairs, including the whole conservative branch, and stops before choosing a coefficient. It refines the card's object from a reserve recurrence to the stopped-range membership each later stage needs first.
bottleneck_link: A later stage can reuse the previous stage's envelope only after its width-w calls are shown to land in that stopped range; the stock coefficient itself remains unbound, so this closes a named piece of the selected stock obligation without claiming the envelope.
stop_rule: Stop after the twelve recorded stage margins and routing rooms, the two published positive controls, the receipt byte binding and the mutation controls. Do not assign a sigma, do not import 57604 or 252, and do not extend to the complex m=73 supplier.
evidence: Exact rational arithmetic on the SHA-256-bound receipt gives floor(s*L_j - L_{j-1}) > 0 for all twelve remaining pairs (native 4-7, conservative 2-7), with the smallest remaining margin 361852943409004062662957360 (native stage 4) and routing rooms floor((1-s)*L_{j-1}). The same code reproduces the published native stage-2 integer 2851485324488315 and stage-3 integer 1015784602045963452130. Controls reject a stale-cutoff substitution (negative at every stage), a cross-branch saving swap (different floors) and a tampered receipt. Every recorded actual_stock_coefficient stays null and the 8194/17 guard is only a comparison.
author: Kumagi (@kumagi), with substantial AI assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash in the OpenCode harness) for reading the predecessors, composing the exact-arithmetic verifier, running an independent recomputation of all margins and rooms, and writing this package. No proof assistant, supplier replay or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Which source sentence bounds the width of a stage-j routing call to the previous stopped algorithm at stages 4-7 (and the conservative branch)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That bound is what would separate the external-factor-1 reading from the hoisted reading at every later stage; without it the stock coefficient stays unresolved even though the calls land in the stopped range.
open_questions.first_step: Match the retained PR185/PR387 cover-row text with a factor c_R whose log2 is at most the smallest routing room floor((1-s)*L_{j-1}) = 4777557234646 native / 4777557267681 conservative.
open_questions.blocked_by: The recorded receipt has the cutoff arithmetic and not that sentence; this package does not invent it.

open_questions.question: Does the selected complex m=73 supplier have an analogous per-stage cutoff sequence whose remaining pairs can be checked the same way?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The complex side binds the selected kappa, so its stock envelope is at least as important as the BIT chain completed here.
open_questions.first_step: Locate the selected complex assembler's own per-stage cutoffs and test whether floor(s*L_j - L_{j-1}) > 0 can be stated for them.
open_questions.blocked_by: No m=73-shaped per-stage receipt is recorded; the stock audit states the selected complex coefficient is uncomputed.

open_questions.question: Do the recorded cutoffs themselves survive a host-side recomputation from the frozen PR1087 assembler instead of the receipt?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would extend byte-level coverage from RESULT.json to the assembler source that produced it, independently of the stock audit's own formula path.
open_questions.first_step: Re-derive a_j, delta_j and L_j from upstream1087.tar.gz's assemble.py lines 205-211 and compare all fourteen cutoffs.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package deliberately does not vendor or execute the frozen assembler; the stock audit already binds that formula, so the gain is byte-level coverage only.
